newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal and European Union start fishing talks.
newsitem.headline: Senegal and European Union start fishing talks.

text.p: Senegal and the European Union (EU) began a fifth round of talks on Sunday to try to reach an elusive new agreement on fishing rights, following a string of failures.

"We are meeting after five months of suspension and we are convinced that this will be the last round, and will be a positive one," Diagua Gueye, head of the Senegalese delegation, told the opening of the talks in the capital Dakar.
The two sides failed in November to agree conditions for renewing their traditional two-year fishing agreement.
"We are determined to go forward and sign very, very fast a new protocol with the European Union," Diagua Gueye added.

During the previous rounds of talks, Senegal was demanding a payment of 18 million European Currency Units (ECUs) to allow EU boats to fish in its waters. The EU offered only 10 million ECUs as compensation.
"I can assure you, that I step into this fifth and, I hope last round, of negotiation with an open mind and with a will to reach an agreement," said Emilio Mastracchio, head of the EU delegation.
Senegal became the first country to sign a protocol of this nature with the EU in 1979.
"Many will not understand after such a long and fruitful cooperation, our talks being deadlocked for so long," Senegal's Diagua Gueye said.
The European Union gave Senegal 31.2 million ECUs for 1992-94 and 15.8 millions ECUs for 1994-96.
